title: Define the daemon inject API contract: `inject:request` / `inject:response` addressed by cwd, reject-if-busy, mTLS-authorized, LRU-deduped
decision: The daemon exposes a new WebSocket message pair `inject:request` and `inject:response` on the existing (post-DEC-000010) mTLS transport. Requests address the target session by its absolute `cwd` (Bosun's role→cwd mapping stays Bosun-side; the daemon has no roles). Responses are synchronous and deterministic: `accepted` when the context was written to the target session's PTY, or `rejected` with one of `busy` / `auth` / `unknown_role`. `not_ready` is collapsed into `unknown_role` in v1 pending a real spawning/unhealthy state in the daemon. Delivery is verbatim (no framing, no trailing newline — the caller composes what the session needs). Authorization gates the handler on the client cert's SAN FQDN appearing in the operator's `injectAllowedClients` config list. Idempotency uses an in-memory LRU keyed on caller-supplied `inject_id` (cap 10k entries, 1 h TTL); the cache does not survive a daemon restart in v1. Governed by `specs/src/daemon/inject-api-spec.md`.

context.task_description: lab-git-manager's Bosun's Mate needs to programmatically inject context into a role's live daemon session and receive a deterministic accept/reject synchronously (terminal outcome arrives out-of-band as a ticket update — not the daemon's concern). The daemon has all the primitives already: sessions indexed by id, cwd tracked per session, IdleDetector maintains a working/idle/needs-attention status, PtyManager.write does raw PTY bytes. This decision pins the message contract that composes those primitives into an external-facing input surface.
assumptions: Bosun's Mate honors a strict 1:1 root-directory-to-role mapping; multiple sessions sharing a cwd is a caller bug and the daemon fails closed (reason='unknown_role').
DEC-000010 (mTLS) has landed before this — client identity is available at message-dispatch time.
PTY writes are kernel-serialized; there is no interleave hazard between concurrent injects into the same session.
1 MB is a reasonable v1 payload cap; larger payloads suggest a design smell on the caller side.

options.label: Reject-if-busy, cwd-addressed, LRU dedupe, verbatim delivery (chosen)
options.description: The handoff's preferred shape (§C reject-if-busy, §F verbatim). Daemon stays a dumb, authenticated pipe for bytes into a PTY. Bosun's Mate handles retry-on-busy in its poll loop. Simplest and matches the caller's stated deterministic-orchestrator invariant.

options.label: Queue-on-busy via the existing `queuedPrompts` machinery
options.description: Reuse the queued-prompt path so injects while a session is `working` deliver on next `needs-attention`. Rejected: introduces silent stacking (two injects while busy → both fire eventually), and the caller has to know the queue depth to reason about ordering. `queuedPrompts` is the right shape for interactive UX, wrong shape for deterministic orchestration.

options.label: Address by session id (composite `daemonId:sessionId`) instead of cwd
options.description: Simpler daemon-side lookup — direct map hit. Rejected: session ids are generated per-spawn and don't survive across a restart/reprovision the way `cwd` does. Bosun's Mate would need a discovery step to resolve role → session id every poll; addressing by cwd removes that.

rationale: Option A minimizes what the daemon knows about Bosun's world (nothing — it just addresses PTYs by cwd), keeps synchronous determinism honest (a single accept/reject with no hidden queuing), and reuses existing primitives (IdleDetector, PtyManager, cert-derived identity from DEC-000010) rather than adding parallel machinery. The rejected options each trade caller determinism for daemon convenience; the handoff is explicit that determinism is the load-bearing property.

risk.rollback: Remove the inject:request / inject:response handling from daemon.ts + transport.ts and delete inject-dedupe.ts. No persisted state to migrate away from. Callers get `UNKNOWN_MESSAGE` on the retired message type.

outcome.notes: Verification: fixture Bosun-Mate client cert + fixture session at a known cwd; each accept/reject branch reproducible in tests; idempotent redelivery of the same inject_id produces one PTY write; unauthorized client cert (SAN not in allowlist) reliably rejected.
